newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NORMAN ANGERED BY JOKE AT HIS EXPENSE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN ANGERED BY JOKE AT HIS EXPENSE.

text.p: A joke at Greg Norman's expense did not sit well with the world's top-ranked golfer on Saturday.

Norman angrily confronted the tournament starter after hitting his third-round opening tee shot at the Kemper Open, following an introduction which included a reference to President Bill Clinton's spill at Norman Florida home.
It is customary at professional tournaments for each player, before starting his round, to be introduced to the gallery by the starter.
Norman was upset that the starter, Bill McGuire, made what he thought was a quip in very poor taste.
After introducing Norman, McGuire paused then added: "If he ever invites you back to his home to inspect his trophy cabinet, you should respectfully decline."
The joke referred to Clinton's visit to Norman's home in March, during which the president snapped a tendon in his right knee that required surgery and left him on crutches.
The gallery roared with laughter, but Norman was furious. After hitting his tee shot he stormed over and told McGuire in no uncertain terms what he thought of the comment.
"Where do you get off saying something like that. Have you ever had anyone injured at your house," Norman said, according to witnesses.
Norman bogeyed the second, third and fourth holes on his way to a two-over-par 73, and at the end of his round refused to talk about the incident.
Tom Lehman, who was paired with Norman, said: "I'm sure the (starter) meant nothing by it. Everyone in the gallery thought it was funny.
"It probably wasn't the time for it," Lehman suggested diplomatically.
"Some guys it wouldn't bother, some guys it would. I think it upset Greg. I saw him in the tent chewing the guy out."
